mainTopic: Whether טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה; a גוי or a קטן putting out a fire on שבת; and covering a lamp, feces, or a scorpion on שבת.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a dispute about a person with השם's name written on his skin who must immerse. The תנא קמא holds that טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה, so we may delay to find a reed to cover the name. רבי יוסי holds it is a מצוה, so the person immerses right away. A ברייתא seems to show רבי יוסי allowing a delay, and the גמרא answers that this is a different רבי יוסי, namely רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Next, a משנה teaches that we neither tell a גוי to put out a fire on שבת nor stop him, but we must stop a Jewish קטן. רבי אמי permits announcing 'whoever puts it out will not lose out.' The גמרא tries to prove this from the משנה and concludes that the משנה proves nothing either way. A ברייתא then tells of יוסף בן סימאי, who refused the soldiers' help, and the חכמים say he did not need to refuse. The גמרא also tries to learn from the קטן rule that בית דין must stop a child from sinning, but רבי יוחנן limits that rule to a child acting for his father. Finally, a new משנה permits covering a lamp, a child's feces, or a scorpion with a bowl, and its גמרא begins a story that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute is about whether immersing on time is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the dispute. The תנא קמא holds טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה, so we look for a reed. רבי יוסי holds it is a מצוה, so we don't look.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The first opinion holds that] immersing at its proper time is not a מצוה, so we go searching for a reed. And רבי יוסי holds that immersing at its proper time is a מצוה, so we do not go searching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation, begun on the previous עמוד, of why the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי argue about a person with השם's name on his skin who needs to immerse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether we may delay the טבילה in order to find a reed to cover the name. If immersing on time is not a מצוה, delaying is fine, so we search for a reed. If immersing on time is a מצוה, we cannot delay, so רבי יוסי says to immerse right away without searching.

keyTerms.meaning: immersing in the מקוה at its proper (earliest) time
a commandment; something we are obligated to do
we go searching (for a reed to cover השם's name)

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The reed is used to cover השם's name written on the skin, so the person doesn't stand undressed in the water with the name uncovered. The real question is whether we may push off the טבילה to go find one.

phrases.english: immersion at its proper time is not a מצוה, and so we search (for a reed);
phrases.notes: This is the view of the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei holds
immersion at its proper time is a מצוה, and so we do not search.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר טְבִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation that began on the previous דף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the underlying principle behind the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two opinions seemed to be arguing only about the practical step of covering the name.
steps.terutzMaskana: They actually argue about whether טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests רבי יוסי allows delaying immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה. A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying that a בעל קרי after מנחה need not immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that immersing on time is a מצוה? But a ברייתא teaches: a זב and זבה, a מצורע and מצורעת, one who had relations with a נדה, and one impure from a dead body all immerse by day [even on יום כיפור]. A נדה and a יולדת immerse at night. A בעל קרי may immerse any time during the whole day. רבי יוסי says: from מנחה time onward he need not immerse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation in step 1. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי seems to say a טבילה may be pushed off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about immersing on יום כיפור, when bathing is normally forbidden. If רבי יוסי lets a בעל קרי skip his טבילה after מנחה and wait until after the fast, then he must hold that טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה. That contradicts what step 1 said about him.

keyTerms.meaning: a man or woman made impure by a certain bodily discharge
a person with צרעת, a spiritual skin affliction
a person made impure by contact with a dead body
a man who had a seminal emission
from the time of the afternoon prayer and onward

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the long list of impure people. The only line that matters for the challenge is the last one: רבי יוסי lets the בעל קרי skip immersing late in the day.

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי טְבִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ מִצְוָה?
phrases.english: But does Rabbi Yosei hold that immersion at its proper time is a מצוה?
But it was taught: a zav and a zavah,
a male leper and a female leper,
one who had relations with a niddah, and one impure from a corpse,
their immersion is by day.
A niddah and a woman after childbirth immerse at night.
One who had an emission may go on immersing
the entire day.
Rabbi Yosei says:
from the afternoon prayer and onward
he need not immerse!
phrases.notes: So רבי יוסי seems to hold that a טבילה may be delayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי טְבִילָה בִּזְמַנָּהּ מִצְוָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion attributed to רבי יוסי in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי lets a בעל קרי push off his טבילה. That only makes sense if טבילה בזמנה is not a מצוה.

steps.title: That ברייתא is a different רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבי יוסי in the ברייתא is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds that a later טבילה is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא follows רבי יוסי the son of רבי יהודה, who said: her last immersion is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by saying the ברייתא is quoting a different רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual רבי יוסי, meaning רבי יוסי בן חלפתא, holds that טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that a late טבילה is good enough ('דייה טבילה באחרונה'), so he naturally allows delaying. That removes the contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: The plain רבי יוסי holds טבילה בזמנה is a מצוה. The ברייתא that allows delay is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds a later טבילה is enough.

phrases.aramaic: הַהִיא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: That one is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: her last immersion is sufficient.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the source to a different תנא with the same name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבי יוסי in the ברייתא is the same רבי יוסי from step 1.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds a later טבילה suffices, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: A non-Jew or a child who comes to put out a fire
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that for a גוי putting out a fire on שבת, we say neither 'put it out' nor 'don't put it out.' A Jewish קטן who comes to put it out is not allowed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a גוי comes to put out a fire, we do not tell him 'put it out' or 'don't put it out,' because his resting is not our responsibility. But if a קטן comes to put it out, we do not listen to him, because his resting is our responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It contrasts a גוי and a Jewish child who come on their own to put out a fire on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We may not tell a גוי to put out the fire, because asking a non-Jew to do מלאכה is forbidden. But we also don't need to stop him, since his שביתה is not our job. A Jewish קטן is different: we are responsible for his שביתה, so we may not let him put out the fire.

keyTerms.meaning: his resting from work on שבת
we do not listen to him (we don't let him do it)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though a קטן is not yet obligated in מצות, the adults are responsible for his not doing מלאכה on שבת. That is why he is treated differently from the גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the difference between אמירה לנכרי, where only an instruction is forbidden, and our responsibility for the שביתה of a Jewish child.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A gentile who comes to extinguish —
we do not say to him 'extinguish' or 'do not extinguish,'
because his resting is not upon them (not their responsibility).
But a child who comes to extinguish —
we do not listen to him,
because his resting is upon them (their responsibility).

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹי שֶׁבָּא לְכַבּוֹת אֵין אוֹמְרִים לוֹ כַּבֵּה וְאַל תְּכַבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; unrelated to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We neither instruct nor stop a גוי putting out a fire. We must stop a Jewish קטן.

steps.title: רבי אמי: one may hint that whoever extinguishes won't lose
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that during a fire, one may announce 'whoever puts it out will not lose out.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: in a fire, they permitted saying, 'Whoever extinguishes will not lose out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי אמי about what one may say during a fire on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A direct instruction to a גוי ('put it out') is forbidden. A general announcement that anyone who helps will be paid is only a hint, and חז״ל permitted it during a fire to save property.

keyTerms.meaning: will not lose out (he will be compensated)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the source for hinting to a גוי in a case of loss, as long as it is not a direct command.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Ami said:
in a fire, they permitted saying
'Whoever extinguishes will not lose out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: בִּדְלֵיקָה הִתִּירוּ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה with a related ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During a fire, an indirect announcement promising payment to whoever extinguishes is permitted.

steps.title: Trying to support רבי אמי from the first clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה supports רבי אמי. It forbids only saying 'כבה', which implies a hint is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה supports him? 'A גוי who comes to put out a fire, we don't tell him כבה or אל תכבה, because his resting is not our responsibility.' It is 'כבה' that we don't say to him. But 'whoever extinguishes will not lose,' we do say to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove רבי אמי's rule by reading the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically forbids the direct word 'כבה'. The suggestion is that if only a direct order is forbidden, then an indirect statement like רבי אמי's must be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say it supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say it supports him:
A gentile who comes to extinguish —
we do not say to him 'extinguish' or 'do not extinguish'
because his resting is not their responsibility.
It is 'extinguish' that we do not say to him;
but 'whoever extinguishes will not lose out' —
we do say to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to support step 5 from the משנה in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's rule permitting 'כל המכבה אינו מפסיד'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The precise wording of the משנה's רישא, which forbids only the direct word 'כבה'

steps.title: The second half of the phrase cuts the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. By the same reasoning, 'אל תכבה' would imply the hint is also not said, so the wording proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the end of the phrase: 'אל תכבה' we don't say to him, and 'whoever extinguishes will not lose' we also don't say to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by looking at the second half of the same phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof read the רישא as saying only the direct order 'כבה' is forbidden, so a hint must be allowed. But by the same reading, forbidding 'אל תכבה' implies that we say nothing to the גוי at all, so the hint 'כל המכבה אינו מפסיד' is forbidden too. The two halves of the phrase point in opposite directions, so the wording proves nothing.

phrases.english: Say the latter part:
'do not extinguish' we do not say to him,
and 'whoever extinguishes will not lose out'
we also do not say to him.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רבי אמי's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference from the רישא is offset by an opposite inference from the סיפא of the same phrase.

steps.title: No proof can be drawn from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה neither supports nor refutes רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the attempted proof and says the משנה cannot decide the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two halves of the phrase point in opposite directions, the משנה's wording proves nothing. רבי אמי's rule stands on its own, without support from this משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: nothing can be learned from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי permits announcing 'כל המכבה אינו מפסיד' during a fire. The משנה neither proves nor disproves this.

phrases.english: Rather, from this nothing can be inferred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the outcome of the rejection in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is inconclusive regarding רבי אמי's permission to hint during a fire.

steps.title: The story of יוסף בן סימאי's fire
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how יוסף בן סימאי refused to let the royal soldiers put out his fire on שבת. A miracle followed, and rain put out the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A fire once broke out on שבת in the courtyard of יוסף בן סימאי in שיחין. Soldiers from the garrison of ציפורי came to put it out, because he was the king's steward. He did not let them, out of respect for שבת. A miracle happened, and rain fell and put out the fire. That evening he sent each soldier two סלעים, and their commander fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a true story about a fire on שבת. The story sets up the חכמים's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soldiers were not Jewish, and they came on their own to help the king's official. יוסף בן סימאי still stopped them because he felt it was not respectful to שבת. The payment after שבת shows he valued their help, even though he refused it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Steward or official who manages property

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident: a fire broke out

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲצֵירוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף בֶּן סִימַאי בְּשִׁיחִין,
phrases.english: in the courtyard of Yosef ben Simai in Shichin,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָאוּ אַנְשֵׁי גִּיסְטְרָא שֶׁל צִיפּוֹרִי לְכַבּוֹת,
phrases.english: and the men of the garrison of Tzippori came to put it out,
because he was the king's steward,
but he did not let them, out of respect for Shabbat;
and a miracle happened for him,
and rain fell and put it out.

phrases.aramaic: לָעֶרֶב שִׁיגֵּר לְכׇל אֶחָד מֵהֶן שְׁתֵּי סְלָעִין,
phrases.english: In the evening he sent each one of them two sela coins,
and to their commander — fifty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After concluding that the משנה neither proves nor refutes רבי אמי, the גמרא brings a ברייתא story connected to the משנה's rule about a גוי putting out a fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף בן סימאי stopped non-Jews from putting out his fire on שבת, out of respect for שבת.

steps.title: The Sages say he did not need to stop them
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say יוסף בן סימאי did not need to refuse. They prove this from our משנה: we tell a גוי neither 'put it out' nor 'don't put it out.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Sages heard about this, they said: He did not need to do that. We learned in the משנה: if a גוי comes to put out a fire, we do not say to him 'put it out,' and we do not say 'don't put it out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים comment on the story. They use our משנה to show that the extra strictness was not required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says we do not stop a גוי who comes on his own to put out a fire. So letting the soldiers act would have been fine, as long as no one asked them. יוסף בן סימאי's refusal was extra piety, not what the law demands.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not need to do that

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the law does not require stopping a גוי who acts on his own initiative. Holding back is allowed as a personal stringency, but it is not an obligation.

phrases.english: And when the Sages heard about the matter, they said:
He did not need to do that,
for we learned:
A non-Jew who comes to put out a fire —
we do not say to him 'Put it out' or 'Do not put it out.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ חֲכָמִים בְּדָבָר, אָמְרוּ: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step comments on the story in step 9 and judges it using the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That יוסף בן סימאי did not need to stop the non-Jewish soldiers
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: גוי שבא לכבות אין אומרים לו כבה ואל תכבה

steps.title: Using the child rule to prove the court must stop a child from sinning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that we do not let a Jewish קטן put out a fire. It suggests this proves that בית דין must stop a child from eating נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: But if a Jewish child comes to put out a fire, we do not listen to him, because his resting is our responsibility. Learn from this: if a child is eating נבלות, בית דין is commanded to stop him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about a קטן. It tries to use that line to solve a separate, well-known question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child is not yet obligated in מצוות, yet the משנה says we must stop him from putting out the fire. That suggests adults must keep a child away from any sin. If so, בית דין must also stop a child who eats forbidden meat.

keyTerms.meaning: A child under the age of מצוות
His resting (on שבת) is their responsibility
Learn from this — introduces a proposed proof
Meat of animals that were not properly slaughtered
To separate him (stop him) from the sin

steps.confusionAlert: The quote of the קטן line is not a new משנה. The גמרא repeats the line from the משנה it is already studying so it can draw an inference from it.

phrases.english: But a child who comes to put out a fire —
we do not listen to him,
because his resting is their responsibility.
Learn from this:
a child who eats unslaughtered meat —
the court is commanded to stop him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא moves from the גוי clause to the next clause of the משנה, about a קטן, and uses it to try to prove a broader rule.
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין must stop a child from eating forbidden food
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: קטן שבא לכבות אין שומעין לו מפני ששביתתו עליהן

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the child is acting for his father
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects the proof. The משנה speaks only of a child who is acting for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The משנה is talking about a child who is acting for his father's sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back the proof from the last step. He says the משנה is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the child puts out the fire to help his father, it is as though the father is having the work done for him. That is why we must stop him. A child who sins on his own, like eating נבלות for himself, is a different case, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: For his father's sake (with his father's interest in mind)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is about a child who acts for his father's sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּקָטָן הָעוֹשֶׂה לְדַעַת אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step rejects the proof in step 11 by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof about stopping a child from eating נבלות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's case may be limited to a child working for his father, so it says nothing about a child sinning for himself.

steps.title: Would the non-Jew also be acting for the Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. If the קטן acts for his father, the גוי in the same משנה should also be acting for the Jew, and that is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same must be true about the גוי: he too would be acting for the Jew's sake. Is that allowed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's reading. It argues that the two parallel cases in the משנה should be read the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי and the קטן appear side by side in the משנה, so they should describe similar situations. If the גוי is putting out the fire for the Jew, it should be forbidden to let him. Yet the משנה says we do not stop him.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same way, the parallel case

phrases.english: Then the same with the non-Jew:
that he acts for the Jew's sake —
is that allowed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step challenges רבי יוחנן's reading from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading that the קטן acts for his father
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel clause about the גוי would have to mean he acts for the Jew. That case is forbidden, yet the משנה permits it.

steps.title: A non-Jew acts for his own sake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a גוי acts for himself, so the two cases are not really parallel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גוי acts for his own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and defends רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי who puts out a fire is presumed to be thinking of his own gain, such as a reward. So he is not doing work for the Jew, and we need not stop him. A child, however, can be acting for his father.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule about the קטן cannot prove that בית דין must stop a child from eating נבלות. רבי יוחנן limits it to a child acting for his father. The גוי is different because he is presumed to act for himself.

phrases.english: A non-Jew acts for his own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the clauses are parallel, the גוי would also be acting for the Jew.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי is presumed to act for his own benefit, while a child can act for his father.

steps.title: The new משנה: covering a lamp, feces, or a scorpion
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה allows overturning a bowl on a lamp, on a child's feces, or on a scorpion on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may overturn a bowl over a lamp so the flame will not catch the ceiling beam. One may also cover a child's feces, and a scorpion so that it will not bite.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three cases where one may cover something with a bowl on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the view of this משנה's תנא, covering is not putting out a fire or trapping. It only prevents harm: fire spreading, a child getting dirty, or a scorpion biting. So the תנא allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: We overturn a bowl (to cover something)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ כּוֹפִין קְעָרָה עַל גַּבֵּי הַנֵּר
phrases.english: MISHNA: One may overturn a bowl over a lamp
so that the fire will not catch the ceiling beam,
and over a child's feces,
and over a scorpion so that it will not bite.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כּוֹפִין קְעָרָה עַל גַּבֵּי הַנֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This opens a new משנה after the fire discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may cover a lamp, a child's feces, or a scorpion with a bowl on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי feared a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells of a case brought to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in ערב. He worried that covering a scorpion might make a person liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: A case came before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in ערב, where someone covered a scorpion. He said: I worry he may owe a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a story that seems to question the last case of the משנה, about covering a scorpion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering a scorpion might count as trapping (צידה), a Torah-level מלאכה. That would require a sin-offering if done by mistake. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was unsure the act was permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The village of ערב in the Galilee
Sin-offering, brought for an accidental Torah violation

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בַּעֲרָב,
phrases.english: A case came before Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai in Arav,
and he said: I am concerned he may be liable for a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה adds a dissenting report about the scorpion case in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי worried that covering a scorpion may make one liable for a חטאת.

steps.title: Three אמוראים visit the house of אבין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story. רב יהודה, רב ירמיה בר אבא, and רב חנן בר רבא came to the house of אבין of נשיקיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה, רב ירמיה בר אבא, and רב חנן בר רבא happened to come to the house of אבין of נשיקיא. For רב יהודה and רב ירמיה בר אבא...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a story. This is a setup line, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scene is only being set here: who was there and where. What happened at the visit, which ties into the משנה's rules, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda and Rav Yirmeya bar Abba
and Rav Chanan bar Rava
happened to come to the house of Avin of Nashikiya.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda and Rav Yirmeya bar Abba...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא וְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי אָבִין דְּמִן נְשִׁיקְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its discussion of the new משנה with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: three אמוראים visited the house of אבין of נשיקיא. The story continues on the next amud.
